architecture: Jerome's own: no VLOOKUP (class factor written per row as a literal), no SUMPRODUCT, one row per part number, scalar arithmetic, aggregates pre-computed in Python and written as literal values, current price hardcoded.

method.formula: weighted_increase = SUM(qty x delta_jpy) / SUM(qty x bp_prior) - 1
method.recipe: in_scope == TRUE AND unpriced_reason IS NULL -> 47,617 rows -> 5.961599%
method.why: The exchange rate and the purchase discount are both already in force, so neither is a forward move.

ebp_evidence.claim: The Export Base Price is built up from IML's own costs, and our purchase price is a discount off it.
ebp_evidence.detail: 62% on vehicle parts and 73.5% on industrial engines, applied to IML's Export Base Price. EBP 1,000 JPY gives a purchase price of 620 JPY on vehicle parts.

ebp_evidence.claim: IML builds its offer price from supplier cost plus a target gross profit.
ebp_evidence.detail: Normal at 25% gross profit, Best at 17%.

ebp_evidence.claim: The discount change and the base-price revision happen at the same moment.
ebp_evidence.detail: Valid from 5 January 2026, "the same timing with annual EBP revision".

ebp_evidence.claim: The base price and the class letter arrive together from Japan.
ebp_evidence.detail: "Please find the B/P, Price Class, and remark as detailed below."

open_items.title: Our configuration carries only the vehicle-parts rate
open_items.detail: config.yaml holds J: 0.673, the vehicle-parts rate. The industrial-engine rate is 73.5% in 2025 and 79.7% in 2026. Our configuration applies 67.3% to everything Japan-sourced.
open_items.action: config.yaml is left alone. Ask IML to confirm the current industrial-engine rate and its part families.

open_items.title: IML states a different revision size from ours
open_items.detail: IML says the CY2026 EBP revision is around 3% for ISZE (weighted average). We measure 5.9616%. Likely different revisions or scopes.
open_items.action: Open reconciliation item. Ask IML for the window, the scope and the weighting behind the 3%.

caveats: The weighted increase is measured on the price comparison itself. No exchange rate and no discount is multiplied into it.
Rows with no source label are reported separately, never assigned to Japan or Thailand.
Volume and mix are held flat. This is the arithmetic of the price move.
CIS current prices sit on the class factors even though the configuration wants a flat 60% margin, so the switch is reported separately.
The result blocks are literal values, computed in Python, so they render the instant the file opens.
